A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Adaptive Width Neural Networks paper, including complete Appendices A–G. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that pages 3–21 are identical; differences on pages 1–2 concern publication-status text, the arXiv stamp, and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original AWNN experiments across tabular, image, graph, and translation tasks in Table 1, plus convergence, compression, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original AWNN experiments in Table 1 and the same main-text and appendix analyses. Retaining these results still qualifies as reporting original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the identical variational objective, neuron-importance rescaling, dynamic width updates, and rescaled weight initialization.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same nine datasets: DoubleMoon, Spiral, SpiralHard, MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, NCI1, REDDIT-B, and Multi30k. No task, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: The fixed-width comparators in Table 1 and the Fixed+ retraining comparator in Appendix D are unchanged within their respective experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C retain identical data splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and model-selection procedures, including Tables 2–5.

E4.justification: The initialization comparison, batch-size and starting-width sensitivity tests, compression analyses, Fixed+ retraining analysis, activation ablations, and graph-layer width plots are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same means and standard deviations over 10 final training runs in Table 1 and retain the same averaging and uncertainty reporting in the appendix results.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are identical, including Appendix D. For example, Table 1 retains REDDIT-B accuracies of 87.0 (4.4) for Fixed and 90.2 (1.3) for AWNN.

T1.justification: The probabilistic formulation, ELBO derivation, Theorem 3.1, and Appendix A's initialization proofs and Lemma A.1 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about learning unbounded width through backpropagation, adapting to task difficulty, and enabling compression through neuron ordering.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the training-overhead discussion in Section 3.3, the bounded-activation recommendation, and explanations of convergence and compression results.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain identical dataset-generation information, hyperparameters, optimizers, schedules, and stopping criteria. The statement that synthetic-data generation code is supplied in supplementary material is also unchanged.

R1.justification: All cited works and the positioning relative to constructive methods, unbounded-depth networks, architecture search, pruning, and distillation remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page notice changes from 'Preliminary work. Under review by the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML).' to 'Preliminary work.' The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened first-page notice accompanies minor spacing and text-flow changes across pages 1–2. All figures, tables, captions, and layouts on pages 3–21 are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 changes only the publication-status notice, arXiv stamp, and opening-page layout. The method, evidence, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—remain identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
